Messages.Author: pd...@lightlink.com
Messages.Body:
Now don't get me wrng here--so far I am quite pleased with the LoB set:
lots of cool new cards and abilities, I love all the new vampires, the
new clans are all cool, a lot of excellent art. All very solid.

After opening about a box yesterday, however, I have been faced with
the ugly reality--this set is simply way too big, in terms of number of
cards. Really, this isn't a huge quibble or anything, but I suspect
that LoB would have been better served by being split into two
different sets:

-Kindred of the Ebony Kingdom
-Bloodlines II: Electric Boogaloo

I have opened about a box of boosters so far, and due to the huge
number of common cards, I have about as many of many commons as I have
of rares (i.e. one). There are no commons that I got more than two of.
I've done pretty well by Vampires, and my Rare selection is reasonable
(a few doubles, a small handfull of Bloodlines reprints), but the
common assortment is kind of abysmal.

Granted, I full well know that this is a CCG and a lot of times you
have to C to get the CG, which is fine. So I'll trade a bunch and buy
common singles. But I think, really, that this particular set would
have been served better by being two different sets--yeah, it's true, I
could just buy 2 boxes of this set instead of, had it been two
different sets, buying a box of each, but there is sooo much in this
set to digest, and it is difficult to digest it all in a reasonable way
with only the 2 or 3 of any given common that you usually want 6-8 of
that you are getting out of a single box.

Again, not a huge issue. I'm hardly outraged or anything. But I think
in the future, sets this immense aren't really that hot of an idea.

-Peter

Would anyone buy the latter? A lot of the Bloodlines stuffs is reprints
and I think that is really your issue. Because one out of four cards
are reprints, you're really buying only 27 packs out of a 36 pack box
containing new stuff, counting new Bloodlines cards.

I'm wondering now if there should even be Bloodlines reprints in LoB.
If White Wolf is reguarly reprinting Bloodlines, then maybe new players
can be told they should get their Bloodlines stuff by just buying
Bloodlines boxes. Of course, the reprints may be better geared to just
the Bloodlines featured in LoB, but I'm wondering if that's a good
enough reason to divert 25% of cards in packs to it.

Of course, one thing I like: the reprints presumedly will be new
layout cards. It will be nice to have the option to play some of the
reprints in the new layout so there will be less mixing of the two
card layout types. I don't think that's really a strong reason by
itself to cause this issue.

> Again, not a huge issue. I'm hardly outraged or anything. But I think
> in the future, sets this immense aren't really that hot of an idea.

Well, perhaps they should not try to take on upgrading and/or printing
new vampires for so many Bloodlines at a time. That would obviate the
need reprint such a high number of old cards. Not to mention arguably
giving short shrift to a Bloodline like Blood Brothers, who apparently
got two common non-unique vampire cards for people to build group 4 Blood
Brothers decks.

Fred

Reprints help draft format. While not as popular as constructed, I
think you might completely kill the chance of being able to draft with
LoB if you left out the reprints. I know the new Blood Brothers are a
bad example because drafting them has its own problems, but since I
looked at their new Sang cards, I know them best. Most of the Sang
cards in this set are to augment the existing cards. If they made no
reprints and you did draft them (ignoring the crypt issues of drafting
them) I think you would be stuck drafting a lot of cards that didn't
get you anywhere in the game by themselves (what are you going to
stealth through with Shell Game if Walk of Caine, Unwholesome Bond and
Coagulated Entity were not reprinted?). I think the other Bloodlines
discipline cards follow along this vein, but I am not sure. I guess you
could draft X packs LoB and Y packs Bloodlines, but then anyone that
drafts any of the Liabon clans is going to get little from the
Bloodline packs.

I think group 4 Blood Brothers are going to be just fine. They already
did the 3 cap and 4x 5 caps in one circle and the 5x 6 caps in another
circle. I don't think another circle of 5 different vamps is really
needed. The options don't seem that appealing, a circle of 7 caps,
while they could have lots of superior disciplines or some interesting
overlapping out of clan disciplines would suffer from being too old to
get out the many Blood Brothers that are normally required to build off
of each other. A circle that ranged in capacity would probably be
pretty good in playability, but that doesn't feel like it fits the
Blood Brother theme to me. Making them C2s would make it easier to get
the 12 needed to put together a crypt, but since they don't seem to be
all that popular, I don't think trading for them will be that difficult
for anyone that wants to build a G4 Blood Brothers deck.

> Fred

Messages.Author: John Flournoy
Messages.Body:
Fred Scott wrote:

> Would anyone buy the latter? A lot of the Bloodlines stuffs is reprints
> and I think that is really your issue. Because one out of four cards
> are reprints, you're really buying only 27 packs out of a 36 pack box
> containing new stuff, counting new Bloodlines cards.

Check your math. Only 27/36 packs on average contain new RARES.

Commons: 120 new commons, of which 49 are reprints. On average you'll
get 3 old cards and 4 new commons. (actually just under 3, but I'll
round it.)
Vampires/Uncommons: 3 in the pack, all of which are new.
Rares: 27/36 are new.

So you're not "really buying only 27 packs out of a 36 pack box
containing new stuff, counting new Bloodlines cards" as you claim, but
REALLY buying 36 packs in a 36 pack box containing multiple new cards,
and most of the time you're getting most of the cards in the pack as
new including the rare.

Oh, but I forgot, only the rares in the pack ever matter to people who
buy cards.

> Fred

-John Flournoy

Bloodlines reprints. If Bloodlines sold really, really well, then we
already have a glut of commons from that set in circulation, right? (I
know I do.) One might ask the question why we would want *more*. Is

after we've all been killed by bird flu and our collections destroyed
so that these newbies would never have been able to aquire these cards?

caused me to only purchase a single box of cards. Normally I'd buy
2-4. This is unfortunate, not for me, but rather for WW.

> common singles. But I think, really, that this particular set would
> have been served better by being two different sets

I agree completely, but this is the set we have. We must make do. I
hope the set does well, but that they do not repeat this strategy.
Save reprints for starters, please.

cmb

Come to think of it, with hindsight, the only thing I would've preferred
to see done differently is to have (roughly) C3s (new cards) and C1s
(reprints) like in the case of the rares.

Before opening anything from Legacies, I felt that I would be bugged by
the reprinted rares, especially those that weren't rares to begin with,

few of most rares.

Yep, that's what I said would be the case a few weeks ago. Reprinted
rares, I can deal with. Especially since I got a Coagulated Entity and
a Darkling Trickery out of the pre-release draft. Reprinted commons,
though I can deal with them, are kind of annoying. C1 reprint commons
and C3 new commons would have been much preferred (assuming that's not
how they did them - if that *is* how they did them, then perhaps
something more drastic would have been in order?).

It would have been nice if, instead of reprinting *everything* from BL,
they would have cut it down to something like 3 commons and 1 rare from
each discipline, or something similar. Just reprint the stuff we need.
I doubt you'd have heard much complaining about dropping Infection,
Clio's Kiss, Brother's Blood, Strength of the Bear, and others (Absorb
the Mind, arguably, although for some reason people seem to think it's
essential for Dominate - however, it's balls for Myt, and none of the 4
new clans have dominate anyway, so it needn't really be in *this* set).

Well, no. You see, I'd buy my usual 2-4 boxes if I wasn't getting
shafted by so many reprints. I bought plenty of the Bloodlines commons
in boxes of that set. I have no need for any more of them. Not
counting rares, I got 96 bloodlines reprints from one booster box of
LoB. 96 per box seems more than excessive to me.

in the process. In fact, if I could have returned the box to the store

actually go out of print. So I'm happy they'll be available for those
players in this set. I'm just very disappointed they're there for me
to get rather than new and intersting things.

multiple displays are less displeased with the low multiples of a given
common, but people who want commons should not have to buy more than
one display.

> Usually you want a common around ten times. Most decks that need more
> of the same common can play with this number. (10 Carrion Crows is
> enough for standard ANI combat, 10 Bonding is enough for a standard DOM
> bleed etc.) So if you only buy one display you want 10 of the same
> commons in one display, if you buy three displays you are happy if you
> only get 4 of the same common with each display.

Why should I hand WW $320 so I can get 10 copies of a *common*. This,
again, is my point.

Some other Jyhad sets had low multiples of each common as well, imho.
This one is extreme; it is thus not worth buying for me. (The boosters,
that is.)

> But your assumption is wrong. You wanted a Laibon Set, but LoB is a
> Laibon/Bloodlines Set.

Your conclusion is wrong. I never made an assumption about LoB. I
decided I was interested the Laibon, I investigated the distribution in
LoB and I found it wanting. I wanted *access* to Laibon cards,
obviously, but that does not require, nor did I assume, a "Laibon" set.

>To moan about that, is like moaning about KMW
> beeing also a independent clan set.

I find your example ironic: I found KMW to be a very good set. Like
LoB, the starters were excellent, but the booster box was good, too. If
LoB had been like KMW, I'd buy LoB boosters.

-- DoR

The first point -- that I can buy singles -- goes without saying. Of
course, because of the size of the set, these are the most expensive
singles I would have ever bought, en masse. So my displeasure with LoB
is not diminished.

And trading for 40+ cards is time consuming and boring -- assuming
success. And that's a pretty stupid assumption, considering that I
would be trading away BL cards, cards already in print, generally
speaking.

I've had to look for commons and a multitude of cards before for other
reasons for other games. If I spend more time trading and buying than
playing, the game isn't worth it. I could be investing in the stock
market for all the fun that is.

Your recommendations do not in any way alieviate my perspective on the
set. Maybe the next one will be better.
